chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan from al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:

A severe drought appeared among the Children of Israel for consecutive years. A woman had a morsel of bread, which she placed in her mouth to eat. The beggar called out, 'O woman of God, hunger!' The woman thought, 'Should I give charity in a time like this?' So she took it out of her mouth and gave it to the beggar. She had a young son who was gathering firewood in the wilderness. The wolf came and carried him off. The cry was raised, and the mother followed in the wolf's tracks. Allah sent Gabriel (peace be upon him) to her, and he took the boy from the wolf's mouth and returned him to his mother. Gabriel said to her, 'O woman of God, are you satisfied with a morsel for a morsel?'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving charity even when one is in need?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) uses this narrative to highlight the principle of *muqabalah* (reciprocal reward), where a single morsel of food given in extreme scarcity is exchanged for the preservation of one's child. The story underscores the spiritual economy of the Hereafter, illustrating how divine generosity often exceeds the material value of the initial act of charity, a theme central to Shia teachings on the efficacy of *Sadaqah*.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 6. It was narrated to me by al-Hassan b. Ahmad from his father from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ibrahim b. Hashim from Musa b. Abi al-Hassan from al-Ridha (a.s.) who said:

Imam Ridha (a.s.) narrates that there was drought in Bani Israel for many years at a stretch. A woman kept a morsel in her mouth. A beggar passed by and called out, “O woman! I am hungry.” The woman thought that she should offer Sadaqah and took out the morsel from her mouth and gave it to the beggar. The woman had a young child who had gone to collect some firewood in the forest. A wolf picked the child up and started running away. The woman started chasing that wolf. Allah sent Jibraeel at that time and he took the child from wolf and returned him to his mother and told her, “O woman! Are you happy to get the return of that morsel through this one?”
